sources.supports: The official storage objectives effective April 17, 2026: Files shares, Blob containers, tiers, Blob/container soft delete, Files snapshots and soft delete, lifecycle management, and versioning. Checked September 20, 2026.

sources.title: Naming and referencing containers, blobs, and metadata
sources.supports: Container length, lowercase and hyphen rules; blob case sensitivity and length; account/container/name identity; flat names and HNS directories.

sources.title: Configure anonymous read access for containers and blobs
sources.supports: Private, Blob, and Container anonymous levels; account-level prohibition overriding container settings; separate management permissions and Microsoft Entra data access.

sources.title: Access tiers for blob data
sources.supports: The complete current four-tier feature table and footnotes: online/offline behavior, relative cost and availability, GPv2 cool/cold 30/90 days versus no such legacy Blob Storage minimum, archive 180 days, LRS/GRS/RA-GRS archive restriction, inferred tiers, premium limitations, and soft-delete billing timing.

sources.title: Blob rehydration from the archive tier
sources.supports: Copy versus in-place tier change, archived previous-version copying, priority and non-instant retrieval, copy completion monitoring, charges, and protection against immediate lifecycle rearchiving.

sources.title: Azure Blob Storage lifecycle management overview
sources.supports: Rule purpose, periodic asynchronous execution, up-to-24-hour policy activation, workload-dependent completion, premium tiering limitations, no archive rehydration, and soft-delete/immutability interactions.

sources.title: Lifecycle management policy structure
sources.supports: Prefix and index-tag filters, case sensitivity and literal wildcard characters, AND filtering, flat-namespace tag limitation, version/snapshot age clocks, strict age comparison, deletion ordering, overlapping actions, and last-tier-change conditions.

sources.title: Manage and find Azure Blob data with blob index tags
sources.supports: Index tags versus metadata and resource tags, current-version tagging, tags retained but not indexed on previous versions, and HNS preview tags not integrated with lifecycle management.

sources.title: Soft delete for blobs
sources.supports: Blob retention 1-365 days, nonretroactive settings, supported overwrite snapshots, undelete behavior with versions, account/container boundaries, HNS deletion and rename/path restrictions, and retained-data billing.

sources.title: Soft delete for containers
sources.supports: Whole-container restoration including versions and snapshots, separate 1-365-day retention, original-name requirement, name-reuse conflict, HNS support, and absence of account-deletion protection.

sources.title: Blob versioning
sources.supports: Supported accounts and write operations, no HNS versioning, immutable version contents, current-blob delete semantics, promotion through copy, interaction with soft delete, disabling behavior, unique-block and explicit-tier billing.

sources.title: Blob Storage feature support in Azure Storage accounts
sources.supports: Current GPv2 and premium block blob compatibility across HNS, Blob NFS 3.0, and SFTP; unsupported versioning and preview snapshot/tag distinctions.

sources.title: Plan an Azure Files deployment
sources.supports: SMB/NFS protocol selection, identity methods, client and network prerequisites, SSD/HDD media, redundancy qualifications, and migration rather than direct HDD-to-SSD conversion.

sources.title: Azure Files management concepts
sources.supports: Generally available classic and standalone resource models; FileStorage versus StorageV2; standalone NFS SSD provisioned v2 model, regional scope, snapshots supported but soft delete unsupported.

sources.title: Create an Azure classic file share
sources.supports: Supported account-kind and SKU combinations, portal creation sequence, protocol and provisioning fields, share naming, backup defaults, and Blob-only account settings that do not configure Azure Files.

sources.title: Understand Azure Files billing
sources.supports: Provisioned v1/v2 versus pay-as-you-go, independent v2 sizing, GiB units, quota versus charged provisioning, HDD transaction optimized/hot/cool trade-offs, tier-change costs and timing limits, retained snapshot/share billing qualifications.

sources.title: NFS Azure file shares
sources.supports: NFS 4.1 SSD and LRS/ZRS restrictions, UNIX permissions and no NFS ACLs or Kerberos authentication, restricted networking, current encryption-in-transit support, and lack of Azure Backup support for NFS.

sources.title: Use share snapshots with Azure Files
sources.supports: Current SMB/NFS and resource-model support, point-in-time read-only share capture and individual-file copying, incremental storage, 200-snapshot limit, deletion dependency, NFS initial-mount requirement and snapshot browsing.

sources.title: Azure file share soft delete
sources.supports: Classic SMB/NFS only, whole-share rather than individual-file recovery, snapshots restored with the share, storage-account-level file setting, retention 1-365 days and original-expiry behavior, and model-dependent billing.

lab.title: Optional manual lab: recover harmless school documents
lab.purpose: Practice object-scope recovery in a trainer-approved disposable account. This is optional and is not executed by the course. The core lessons already explain every required decision; no production data or real pupil records are needed.
prerequisites: A trainer-approved disposable standard GPv2 StorageV2 account with flat namespace, hot Blob default, LRS, and HDD pay-as-you-go classic SMB shares available. Use an existing lab account dedicated to this exercise, not an account containing other users' data.

An authorized identity with the management permissions needed for account data-protection settings, containers, and classic shares, plus separately sufficient Blob/File data permissions for the chosen portal access method. Do not grant or reveal account keys merely to bypass missing permissions.

An approved network path and browser. An actual SMB mount additionally requires a supported client, permitted TCP 445 or approved private connectivity, correct DNS, and preconfigured SMB authentication and permissions.
Two harmless local text files containing clearly different text, such as timetable version one and timetable version two. Record the exact lab resource names before changing anything.
Approval for retention-related charges and a cleanup owner. Skip Azure execution and trace the lesson examples on paper if no subscription, budget, or permitted access is available.
lab.costWarning: Azure can charge for stored data, versions, snapshots, soft-deleted contents, and operations even in a small lab. Do not archive data, deploy VMs, add private endpoints, enable a backup vault, or purchase provisioned capacity merely for this exercise. The portal can offer Backup by default when creating a share; deliberately opt out for this dedicated short-lived lab if approved. Retention may keep charging after logical deletion. No fixed price or free entitlement is assumed.
steps: Record the lab account and all current settings. In Data protection, verify or enable seven-day blob soft delete, seven-day container soft delete, and blob versioning. Separately verify or enable seven-day file-share soft delete. These settings are account-wide within their service, which is why the account must be dedicated.

Create the private container school-recovery-lab with account-level anonymous Blob access still disabled. Upload the first harmless text file as timetable.txt and record its actual version identifier, length, and hot tier.

Overwrite timetable.txt with the second content. Show versions and confirm the first is previous and the second current. Read the previous contents, then use the portal's supported promote/copy operation to make those verified contents current again. Confirm a new current version exists rather than assuming the old identifier changed.

Delete only the current base blob, leaving previous versions. Observe the missing current object and retained history. Copy the verified first contents back to the base name and confirm an ordinary authorized read succeeds.
Delete only school-recovery-lab, show deleted containers, and restore that exact container before reusing its name. Verify the expected blob and versions are present.

Create the classic SMB share office-recovery-lab in the approved pay-as-you-go account. Use a 1 GiB quota if accepted for that lab account, otherwise the smallest approved quota; this is not provisioned purchasing. Keep transaction optimized for the short exercise and review the optional Backup setting without provisioning a vault.
Upload the first harmless timetable file to the share through the permitted portal data path. Create a share snapshot, record its timestamp, then overwrite the live file with the second content.

Browse the snapshot, verify the earlier contents, and restore only the timetable file. Reopen the live file. If an approved SMB mount is already available, repeat the read through that client to distinguish portal access from mounted-share access.

Delete only office-recovery-lab with its snapshots as required by the portal workflow. Show deleted shares, select the recorded share instance, and undelete it. Confirm Active status, the live timetable, and the retained snapshot.

Write a paper lifecycle rule selecting only school-recovery-lab/ with an appropriate test tag and a current-blob modification age greater than 30 days. Predict which newly created lab objects match now. Do not enable automatic deletion or wait weeks for an age transition merely to finish this lab.

Record the differences between version promotion, container restore, snapshot file restore, and share undelete. Follow the narrow cleanup checklist and confirm who will track any retained-data charges until expiry.
expectedResults: The private container supports authorized reads without anonymous access. Overwriting the block blob creates history, and copying old contents produces a new current version.
Deleting the current version leaves previous versions; deleting and restoring the whole container demonstrates its separate recovery scope.
The share snapshot contains the earlier text and can restore only that file without changing unrelated live files.
Classic share undelete restores the whole share and its snapshot. It does not demonstrate individual-file undelete, which share soft delete does not provide.
The newly created sample does not meet the paper lifecycle age threshold, and no archive rehydration or automatic destructive policy has been executed.
cleanup: Remove only the recorded test blob versions, test container, test share, and its test snapshots when they are no longer needed. Deletion may leave recoverable retained objects and charges until their configured expiry.

Do not disable protection globally, shorten another user's retention, remove production locks, or delete an unrelated resource group to force immediate cleanup. If the account is genuinely lab-only, let its authorized owner decide its final disposal after verifying nothing else depends on it.
Remove only lab-created mounts, cached lab connections, and the harmless local sample files. Do not remove pre-existing network, identity, or backup configuration.

Recheck the lab account's active and deleted-object views and record the expected retention expiry. Confirm the cleanup owner will review remaining storage costs rather than claiming that an empty normal listing proves zero retained data.
